mechanisms.behavior: A-18581 crank and drive plate oscillate the A-19112 gun using one 12V motor (20). Position switch76 marks the near-backbox end before counter-clockwise travel. Coil3 fires a chambered ball sensed by opto44. Trapdoor high8 and hold16 admit a ball into the under-playfield mini-trough, where mechanical77 and opto45 sense its passage and arrival; coil5 pops it through the loading tube to44. At rest the door is closed and chamber empty; the gun parks by position feedback during startup homing. T.17 runs motor20 on Up and stops it on Down or timeout. Fresh static and periodic position-feedback probes both timed motor20 out after about24.600 elapsed harness seconds; the manual calls this about20seconds. The test gently ejects a chambered ball. A blocked or misadjusted76 prevents correct homing; failed45/77/44 feedback interrupts loading, so do not replace one sensor with another. The retained script uses a simplified angular model and writes77 from motor state; its angles, timing and lockup substitution are recreation details rather than physical feedback. See the knowledge note for clean-state traces and failure behavior.
mechanisms.label: Motorized .44 Magnum and loading system

mechanisms.behavior: Four physical balls occupy slots32-35 at rest;31 is a separate jam/exit opto. Ball-release1 feeds the shooter lane15,then autoplunger2 sends the ball into the launch path. Let balls move through the optos; an asserted jam sensor is not the normal empty exit. The table's cvpmBallStack derives the slots from a count and pulses31 only from a full stack,a simplification of the physical five-opto trough. A stuck occupied slot or jam prevents reliable accounting and serve. Trigger11 requests launch in normal play.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball outhole trough and autolaunch

mechanisms.behavior: WarehouseEntry captures a ball into the under-playfield opto46 and coil4 ejects it back through sw46 onto its ramp. The script's Warehousedw is an anti-double-ball simulation barrier; it is not the removed sample drop target. Production coil4 is AE-23-800,corrected by the amendment.
mechanisms.label: Warehouse entrance and top-right popper

mechanisms.behavior: HQHole drops the ball under the playfield into opto47. Coil14 ejects through the separately positioned sw47 kicker to play. The visible receiving hole and hidden outlet are separate locations; collisions determine ball feed,not a coil-to-switch direct relationship.
mechanisms.label: HQ hole and left popper

mechanisms.behavior: Switch73 detects the captured ball; coil26 ejects it. Script bsSafeHouse uses the sw73 saucer and a tuned kick,which supplies runtime routing without establishing physical launch speed.
mechanisms.label: Safehouse saucer / top-left popper

mechanisms.behavior: Coil15 changes the right ramp route through diverterR. The table animates a flipper-like diverter and its blade,returning when off. The physical assembly is A-18585; its geometry and return spring define the route. There is no separate matrix-position sensor.
mechanisms.label: Right ramp diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Coil27 operates A-19746. SolDiverterHold alternates the DiverterOFF and DiverterOn/On2 collision surfaces; these are one physical route selector,not three actuators. Default is DiverterOFF enabled and the two On surfaces dropped.
mechanisms.label: Left diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Gate28 opens the right-loop gate while energized. Magnet35 under the loop catches and releases a ball to give a slow feed to the upper-right flipper; the ROM's Magnet Test pairs right-loop opto42 with35. The magnet is the repurposed upper-left power circuit,not a fourth flipper. Gate and magnet are distinct devices even when used in the same ball path.
mechanisms.label: Right-loop controlled gate and Magna Force magnet

mechanisms.behavior: Historical sample hardware only: amendment16-10007 removes drop-down6,drop-reset25,left-loop gate36 and switch53; production table calls each unused. The same LX-2 firmware retains their test names and pulses,including6during initialization. No production load or separate machine/driver grouping is invented. The unique parts list retains A-19724 Drop Target & Decal; this historical listing does not override the amendment. Physical sample geometry/travel and any unretained sample settings remain outside the production recreation contract.
mechanisms.label: Removed sample warehouse drop target and left-loop gate

mechanisms.behavior: One FL-11629 blue coil has power and hold windings,with a normally-open EOS closing near the end of stroke. The ROM drives the windings separately; PinMAME's power callback aggregates both. The physical EOS exists,while core_updateSw synthesizes its public state; consumers drive button inputs,not EOS. The old table's right-flipper routine moves both right flippers together,a simulation simplification of the independent ROM upper outputs.
mechanisms.label: Lower-right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: Ball contact with the left rubber closes leaf switch61; the A-17811 crank and AE-26-1200 coil9 kick the ball away. Plunger02-2364, link03-8085 and crankA-12664 form one arm mechanism; spring10-128 returns it after the pulse. Default is released, with the contact open when no ball deflects the rubber. The T.1 service probe at switch61=1 observes a pulse at9; this is not a physical stroke-time measurement. Keep the leaf contact and arm free to return; a stuck contact is a fault, not a motor-position sensor. The VPX animation timer and tuned wall force are recreation choices.
mechanisms.label: Left slingshot

mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Ball movement of the left jet wafer closes leaf switch63. AE-26-1200 coil11 in A-9415-2 moves the plunger and linked A-4754 ring to rebound the ball. Springs10-7 and10-326 restore the wafer/armature after the pulse; rest has the contact open. T.1 switch63=1 produces a pulse at11; no physical pulse width, ring travel time or startup kick is asserted. A stuck leaf or binding wafer/ring is a fault, not a separate home sensor. The assembly has a #555 wedge socket, but the retained page does not assign its GI string; do not substitute separate matrix dome lamps84/85. VPX timer/force values are recreation tuning.
mechanisms.label: Left jet bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Ball movement of the middle jet wafer closes leaf switch64. AE-26-1200 coil12 in A-9415-2 moves the plunger and linked A-4754 ring to rebound the ball. Springs10-7 and10-326 restore the wafer/armature after the pulse; rest has the contact open. T.1 switch64=1 produces a pulse at12; no physical pulse width, ring travel time or startup kick is asserted. A stuck leaf or binding wafer/ring is a fault, not a separate home sensor. The assembly has a #555 wedge socket, but the retained page does not assign its GI string; do not substitute separate matrix dome lamps84/85. VPX timer/force values are recreation tuning.
mechanisms.label: Middle jet bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Ball movement of the right jet wafer closes leaf switch65. AE-26-1200 coil13 in A-9415-2 moves the plunger and linked A-4754 ring to rebound the ball. Springs10-7 and10-326 restore the wafer/armature after the pulse; rest has the contact open. T.1 switch65=1 produces a pulse at13; no physical pulse width, ring travel time or startup kick is asserted. A stuck leaf or binding wafer/ring is a fault, not a separate home sensor. The assembly has a #555 wedge socket, but the retained page does not assign its GI string; do not substitute separate matrix dome lamps84/85. VPX timer/force values are recreation tuning.
mechanisms.label: Right jet bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Pendulum03-8668 and wire12-6231 carry plumb bob20-6502-A inside lower bracket01-3445. Cabinet movement brings the bob/contact together; at rest the normally-open contact is clear. This is tilt14, distinct from slam tilt21. It has no coil, automatic homing output or software-driven physical reset; let the pendulum settle and keep it clear of the contact bracket. Sensitivity depends on physical adjustment rather than an invented timed switch pulse.
mechanisms.label: Plumb-bob tilt

mechanisms.behavior: AE-23-800 coil7 moves A-5387 plunger in the cabinet knocker; one momentary activation makes the physical strike. Rest is de-energized. There is no matrix position sensor, ball path or home-feedback input. T.4 names and pulses this output; the table plays a sound but does not represent physical plunger travel. Do not hold the coil continuously or invent feedback from an unrelated switch.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet knocker

Virtual J111 GPIO bit5. PinMAME publishes WPC_GILAMPS bit5 here; observed in the retained boot/service runs. No physical coil29 exists: printed29 is the lower-right power winding at public45.

Virtual J111 GPIO bit6. Core unconditionally exposes WPC_GILAMPS bit6 at public30, the same state-channel contract as bit5 at29. This identifies transport, not a production coil or an asserted game-specific function. No30 transition was observed in the retained probes; that does not make this published state unused. Physical printed30 is lower-right hold at public46; it does not bind here.
Virtual WPC_GILAMPS bit7 mirror. This driver has no fast-flip RAM address, so it is the legacy GameOn/J111 state, not a direct physical coil. Printed31 is lower-left power at public47.
Reserved core bit11; wpc.c stores only bits8-10 from WPC_GILAMPS (no fastflip on dh), so this is constant zero. Printed32 is lower-left hold at public48.
